profile: 60 paid journeys/s for 60 s; two synchronized generator processes; 0.2 s polling; four API replicas and four Kafka consumers; 500 total in-flight; eight simulator threads; 12 DB pool waiters per API; one callback/payment; zero retries; four-route HTTP transport trace
transport_phase_p95_ms_mode: worst shard p95, not combined percentile; GET figures extracted from per-shard records because the original aggregate covered hold/payment only
interpretation: Both status GET classes, hold and payment spend seconds before sending headers, while response-header waits are tens to hundreds of milliseconds. This establishes a shared pre-send bottleneck in the synthetic HTTP client path, without proving its exact internal cause. Concurrent API DB-pool rejections are a separate real backend failure. The stage cannot establish 60/s capacity or one-hour paid-ticket throughput.
